newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes weak, but MidEast premiums heard firm.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes weak, but MidEast premiums heard firm.

text.p: Cash crude prices in Asia were lower on Tuesday in line with the overnight slump in futures prices, but Middle East premiums were heard steady to firmer.
Another Oman cargo was heard traded into China by a trader at MPM +28 cents -- in line with recent deals and reflecting the generally firm tone of medium grades. The deal was not confirmed.
A 500-600,000-barrel cargo of Qatar Marine was heard traded at QGPC +48 cents between an equity holder and a Japanese trader.
The price surprised some traders who had expected the market to trade lower as Japan and South Korea switch into more medium grades for the spring season.
In addition, some traders said Japan throughput was likely to decline as it moves away from a heavy middle distillate gearing.
Elsewhere, prices showed the signs of the Brent and NYMEX futures, which slumped overnight on warmer weather concerns in the U.S. northeast.
Brent/Dubai spreads for March came in to $1.85/$1.92 from $1.90/$2.00 per barrel in New York. The March/April Dubai came in to 45/51 cents from a day-earlier 50/55 cents.
Paper Tapis, which largely bucked the falling futures trend late last week, dropped 70 cents to be quoted at $24.60/$24.79 per barrel.
The lower prices sparked a May Tapis swap deal covering 200,000 barrels at $22.75. A U.S. bank was the seller and a U.S. trader the buyer.
